subject.lede: Part of the 100x plugin overview (explain/100x-plugin). Think of a building inspector with a camera. First the inspector photographs the site exactly as it stands (the snapshot, pinned to one commit), so every note says "this beam, in this photo" and a later change to the site cannot make a note point at the wrong beam. The notes go into one logbook (review.json), and every report anyone reads is printed from it. A clerk (the gate) checks the paperwork before anything goes out. Nothing is mailed to the builder until you have read the exact letter and said yes, and even then it goes as a draft only you can see. Only one door in the building opens onto GitHub, and it is the skill's own written steps, not the tools.

tldr.what: Turns a pull request link into review comments you read and adjust, then posts them to GitHub as a draft only after you say yes.
tldr.how: A snapshot pins the reviewed commit, agents write findings into one record, every file is rendered from it, a gate checks it, and posting re-checks the commit first.
tldr.watch_out: The rule that nothing posts without your yes lives in the skill's steps, not in code; the draft default is what limits a mistake.

context.purpose: Give Claude a pull request link and get review comments you can read, change and then post to GitHub as a draft only you see, each pointing at the exact commit that was reviewed, with nothing sent until you say yes.
context.why_now: This is the one part of the plugin allowed to write to GitHub, so where that door is, and what guards it, is worth seeing step by step.
in_scope: The three commands, in order: review, adjust, post
Where the output lands, and why never inside the reviewed repo
How the snapshot pins the head commit, and how the gate holds links to it
One record per PR, and every readable file rendered from it
The post flow: the commit check, the exact payload, one explicit yes, a draft
Why gh runs only from the skill's steps (the decision record on gh in decisions/)
The snapshot, review and gate functions in the Code reference
out_of_scope: How reviewers judge the code (diff-review and stack-reviewer)
The adjust command's edit rules in detail
Checking that a suggested change applies (pr_suggest)

entry_points.label: /pr-review adjust <pr-url>
entry_points.note: edits only the user blocks in review.json, then renders and gates again; not animated

entry_points.label: /pr-review init
entry_points.note: scaffolds the review folder without reviewing a PR; the review command runs it first

entry_points.note: the check run before reporting and again before posting

terms.means: The exact commit at the tip of the PR when it was reviewed, {{sha_len}} long. Every link and line claim points at it, so a later push cannot shift them.
Copies of the PR's files at the head, at the merge-base and on the default branch, plus the diff, exported from git into a scratch folder.
One point in review.json: what is wrong, where, how sure the reviewer is, what to change and who should answer.
Writing a file a person reads (README, comments to post, questions, the GitHub payload) from review.json by code, never by hand.
The checker for a review folder: shape, links, evidence labels and rendered files. It must pass before the review is reported and again before posting.
Where every review of one repo lives: by default beside your clone, never inside it. Called CR in the skill.
One review run's folder inside the review folder; a re-review of the same PR gets a new dated one.
A separate Claude agent that reviews the PR from one angle (security, design, missed scenarios) and returns its findings for merging.
GitHub's own command-line tool. It keeps your login per host, so GitHub Enterprise works the same as github.com.
Before posting, the PR's current head commit is compared with the reviewed one; any difference stops the post.
The only answer that posts. Anything else, a question back or silence included, posts nothing.
A GitHub review sent without an event: it stays pending, visible only to you, until you submit it on the PR.

lines.code: git fetch --quiet remote                     # the only call that changes the clone
git fetch remote pull/<n>/head; sha = FETCH_HEAD
write PINS.md: base, head SHA, merge-base, commits, files, behind
if gh head SHA != review.json pr.head_sha: stop, re-review
payload = pr_review emit <pr-dir> draft      # no event -> pending
show every inline comment and the general ones; ask once
if answer is not an explicit yes: post nothing

diagrams.title: What the pr-review skill is made of
diagrams.source:
mindmap
  %% level: 2
  root((pr-review))
    Skill steps
      gh, read only while reviewing
      post after one yes
    Snapshot
      head SHA pinned
      trees and diff
    One record

    Output

diagrams.caption: Read outward from the centre: the skill's steps are the only part that talks to GitHub; the tools pin, record, render and check.

diagrams.title: Where the review folder lands, first match wins
diagrams.caption: Every branch ends outside the reviewed repo: the fallback is the user's own folder, so a review is never written into someone else's working tree.

diagrams.title: Posting, call by call
diagrams.source:
sequenceDiagram
  %% level: 2
  actor You
  participant Claude
  participant Tool as pr_review
  participant Gh as gh
  participant GitHub
  You->>Claude: post this PR
  Claude->>Gh: head SHA of the PR now
  Gh->>GitHub: read the PR
  GitHub-->>Gh: current head SHA
  Gh-->>Claude: current head SHA
  alt head moved since the review
    Claude-->>You: stop, re-review first
  else head unchanged
    Claude->>Tool: emit draft payload
    Tool-->>Claude: review JSON and a preview
    Claude->>You: exact text, post as a draft?
    alt you say yes
      Claude->>Gh: create the review with no event
      Gh->>GitHub: pending review, visible only to you
      Claude->>Tool: mark the items posted
    else anything else
      Claude-->>You: nothing posted
    end
  end
diagrams.caption: Two stops guard the one write: a moved head ends it before the payload is built, and anything short of a yes ends it before gh is called.

scenarios.title: From a PR link to a draft review on GitHub

steps.t: You give Claude a pull request link
steps.d: Any github.com or GitHub Enterprise PR URL; host, owner and repo are read from it, never typed.

steps.t: Claude works out the review folder, outside the reviewed repo
steps.d: First match wins: a flag, an environment variable, git config, your config file, else beside the clone. The answer says which rule chose it.
do: review folder and the rule that chose it

steps.t: Claude reads the PR's details through gh, read only
steps.d: While reviewing, gh only reads: the PR, its checks, linked issues and existing comments.

steps.t: pr_snapshot pins the head SHA and exports the trees
steps.d: It fetches the PR's head from the remote, records its exact commit, and exports the head, the merge-base and the default branch, plus the diff. The clone is fetched into, never checked out.

steps.t: Claude starts every reviewer agent in one message
steps.d: Up to {{max_agents}}, all in the background, each reading the snapshot rather than the moving branch.

steps.t: The agents finish and their findings merge into review.json
steps.d: Each point becomes one item. A lens with more than {{lens_cap}} is refused, with nothing written.

steps.t: pr_review renders every file a person reads from review.json
steps.d: README, the comments to post, the questions and the GitHub payload all come from the one record, so they cannot disagree.

steps.t: The gate checks links, the snapshot and the rendered files
steps.d: Every link must sit on this repo at the pinned commit, every cited line must exist in the snapshot, and every rendered file must equal a fresh render.

steps.t: Claude reports and stops: a review run never posts
steps.d: It ends with the loop: read the README and the comments, adjust anything, then post.

steps.t: Later you say post; the head SHA must not have moved
steps.d: Claude runs the gate again, then asks gh for the PR's current head and compares it with the reviewed one.
code: if gh head SHA != pr.head_sha: stop

steps.t: Claude shows the exact payload and asks once
steps.d: The payload has no event, so GitHub keeps it pending. A summary over {{body_max}} gets a warning. Anything but an explicit yes posts nothing.

steps.t: gh creates the draft review and the record marks each item posted
steps.d: The draft is visible only to you until you submit it on GitHub; posted items are never sent again.

scenarios.title: The author pushed after the review: post stops

steps.t: You say post, but the PR's head is a newer commit than the reviewed one
Claude stops; no payload is built and nothing is posted
steps.d: A comment pinned to the old commit could point at lines that have since changed.

steps.t: A re-review gets a new dated run, carrying your edits forward
steps.d: Your skips and rewordings, and anything already posted, are copied into the new record unchanged.

scenarios.title: What if the tools called gh themselves?

steps.t: The agents' findings are merged and ready to render
The render tool calls gh and posts as soon as the files are written
The author sees comments you never read
do: comments already visible to the author

steps.t: Every test of the tools now needs a fake gh and a login per host
do: a network write inside the tools, and a gh mock in every test

scenarios.title: Fix: the tools only read and render; gh runs only from the skill's steps

steps.t: pr_review only renders: no gh call and no HTTP code in any pr-review script
gh is a dependency of the skill's steps only, and writes in exactly one place
steps.d: That place is post, after you have seen the exact payload and said yes.
do: gh: read-only while reviewing; one write, in post

steps.t: The review run ends with you reading it

scenarios.title: No code stops an agent that ignores the skill from posting

steps.t: An agent that skips the skill's rules runs the post command itself
Nothing intercepts it: the boundary is a written rule, not code
steps.d: The safety audit scans the tools, not the skill's steps, and the command guard does not watch review posts.
do: no hook or audit sees gh posting a review

steps.t: The draft default limits the damage: only you see it until you submit

options.label: gh, called only from the skill's written steps
pros: The tools stay standard-library Python and git, testable offline
gh already owns the login per host, so GitHub Enterprise needs no token handling
cons: The skill does not work without gh and a login per host
No code can check that post waited for a yes

options.label: Call the GitHub API from the tools with the standard library
cons: Re-implements tokens and Enterprise API addresses
Puts a network-writing path inside the tools the safety audit promises never send anything

options.label: Run gh from inside the tools
pros: One place for every GitHub call
cons: A hidden runtime dependency in tools that must run anywhere
Every test needs a fake gh

options.label: Never post; you paste comments by hand
pros: Nothing can ever post by mistake
cons: Drops the draft review and the lost-summary recovery the workflow exists for

decision.deciding_factor: The tools promise to use only the standard library and git and to send nothing, so the one GitHub write had to be admitted deliberately in the skill, where you see it, not leak into the tools.
decision.revisit_when: A tool needs GitHub data a skill step cannot pass it as a file or argument, or a request to post automatically is accepted.

checks.q: The review was written yesterday. What is checked before anything is posted?
checks.answer: The gate runs again, and the PR's current head commit must equal the one the review pinned; otherwise post stops.

checks.q: The head moved. Does Claude post the old comments anyway?
checks.answer: No: it stops before building the payload and suggests a re-review, which carries your edits forward.

checks.q: Which part of the plugin is allowed to write to GitHub?
checks.answer: Only the skill's post step, through gh, after you have seen the exact payload and said yes. No script calls gh.

notes.GitError: The one error the tool raises: a named git failure, printed and turned into exit code one.
notes.git: Runs one git command in the clone and returns its output, raising a named error on failure.
notes.git_ok: The same git call, returning nothing instead of raising when it fails.
notes.pick_remote: Chooses the remote: the one named, else the one whose URL matches the PR, else the only one, else upstream, else origin.
notes.default_branch: Finds the remote's default branch from its HEAD ref, then from the server, then main or master; otherwise fails and asks for a base.
notes.snapshot: Fetches, then for each PR records the head commit and merge-base, exports the head, base and default trees and the diff, and writes PINS.md.
notes.main: Parses the flags, runs the snapshot, prints PINS.md, and exits with failure on a git error.

notes.find: Prints every earlier review of a PR in the review folder, newest first; exits with failure when there is none.
notes.next_run: Prints the next dated run folder for a re-review, adding a counter when one already exists today.
notes.merge: Adds reviewer fragments' items to review.json, skipping duplicates of another item and refusing a lens over its cap.
notes.render_pr: Renders README, comments to post, questions and the GitHub payload from one review record.
notes.write_pr: Writes those rendered files into the PR folder and refreshes the rendered regions of the findings file.
notes.github_review: Builds the GitHub review payload: inline comments on diff lines, general ones in the body, pinned to the head commit; an event only when asked.
notes.preview: Prints what post would send, item by item, and what is skipped or left for you to send by hand.
notes.emit: Prints the payload for a draft or a submit, a preview on stderr, and a warning when the summary is long; exits early when nothing is new.
notes.mark_posted: Records a successful post on each sent item and in the run's post list, keeping the summary in case a draft loses it.

notes.check_schema: Checks the record's shape: summary, run, item ids, kinds, severities, statuses, and the user and posted blocks.
notes.check_items: Checks each item reads plainly, holds a real value, links only to this repo at the pinned commit, and that existing PR comments were read first.
notes.check_pr_meta: The PR URL must be a real pull URL whose number matches, and the head must be a full commit hash.
notes.check_snapshot: Against the snapshot: each cited file and line exists at the head, the in-diff flag is right, a suggestion sits on a diff line and changes something, a diff removes only real lines.
notes.check_rendered: Every rendered file must equal a fresh render of review.json; a hand edit fails.
notes.check_readme: The README's who-reviewed table is complete and its action table lists exactly the open, not-skipped items.
notes.check_pr: Runs every rule on one PR folder, stopping after the shape check if the shape is wrong.
notes.check_root: Checks a run root: its pins file, each PR folder, and that the feature README equals a fresh render.
notes.main: Picks a PR folder or a run root, runs the rules and the mermaid check, and passes only when both pass.
